description: What decision: validation.rs forbidden() closure explicitly checks c as u32 <= 0x20 (all C0 controls + space) and c as u32 == 0x7f, rather than using char::is_whitespace(). A doc comment explains why: Rust's is_whitespace() does not match NUL (\x00), but NUL in a Message-ID would corrupt canonical serialisation (the serialiser uses \x00\n as header/body separator) and break C-string APIs downstream. Why right: the explicit bounds make the security invariant auditable at a glance without reading is_whitespace() docs. The doc comment names the downstream corruption mechanism (canonical serialiser separator), making the constraint self-explaining. Alternatives rejected: (1) is_whitespace() alone — silently passes NUL; (2) regex — heavier dependency with no benefit here; (3) allowlist of valid chars — more restrictive than RFC 5322 intends for the non-structural chars.
title: DECISION: NUL-byte check explicit in is_valid_message_id rather than relying on is_whitespace()
